utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. My apologies for delaying everybody. I was caught up with another matter. If I could remind you, Mr. Tucker, that the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would kindly ask to you go back into your binder under tab 19. This is document 1D191. It is an exhibit now, and it is the letter of agreement that was sent by or on behalf of Patrick Lopez-Terres on the 20th of February of 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll kindly ask the registry to turn to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker I simply want to go through a number of other conditions which was set by the Office of the Prosecutor to the Macedonian authorities. I will ask you to look at condition number 10. That's on the second page, Mr. Tucker. It says this: "The Republic of Macedonia authorities undertake to ensure the integrity of any mortal and physical evidence gathered to the highest professional standards and to the satisfaction of the OTP representatives." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the next condition, condition 11, it says that: "The Republic of Macedonia authorities undertake to supply to representatives of the OTP copies of all investigation documents associated with the investigation." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Now, at the very end of the letter, Mr. Lopez-Terres says that: "I wish to thank you for your cooperation in moving this issue forward. I am sure you will agree it is in the interest of all parties to address this issue as expeditiously as possible. I hope that this initiative will in some way contribute to the future stability in the region." I'd now ask you to turn to another document in your binder, which is tab 28 [sic], and it is Rule 65 ter 1D51 -- 587, I apologise. Do you agree, Mr. Tucker, that this appears to a letter coming from the public prosecution office of the Republic of Macedonia. It is dated the 25th of February of 2002, so five days after the letter of Mr. Lopez-Terres. It is being sent to the Office of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, and it is addressed to Madam Del Ponte. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry. Simply, my tab 28 is an investigator note of Mr. Tucker. I'm wondering--

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: 20 A, Mr. Saxon. "A" like Alan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: 20 A, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree, Mr. Tucker, that this letter is signed by the public prosecutor of Macedonia, Mr. Dzikov; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look at the text of that letter, you will agree that Mr. Dzikov informed your office, more specifically Madam Del Ponte, that: "We inform you that we are agreeable with the conditions for exhumation and further court and investigative procedures." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then he closes his letter with the words: "With all respect and hope for our further mutual cooperation." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence would seek to tender this letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D200 Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, you would agree that the conditions which were set by the Office of the Prosecutor for its participation in the exhumation procedure impacted not only on the competencies and mandate of the state prosecutor, but also upon other state organs, including the Macedonian Security Forces. You would agree with?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That again, sir, I would agree to a point, and I think I should, if you allow me, elaborate a little bit. When discussing conditions set by the Office of the Prosecutor, the conditions referred to the letter of the agreement relate to issues that are sensitive on all sides, both the authorities of Macedonia and for the relatives of the deceased. It was is fact that the relatives of deceased refused to cooperate through mistrust of the authorities of Macedonia. And the Macedonian authorities were unable, without the risk of future conflict, to go into the region in order to conduct their investigation into the -- into the deaths of the -- of those victims and to conduct the exhumation. The role of the Office of the Prosecutor was to try to find a compromise by all parties would be agreeable to this operation moving forward. So the conditions that are mentioned are not the conditions of the Office of the Prosecutor but, rather, the conditions that all parties would agree to, to take this motion forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, indeed, we've seen that the conditions were all greed upon by the authorities that I just showed you in this letter?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, I will go into a number of issues which you just indicated as to the steps you which took to facilitate that matter, but going back -- a step backward to my previous question. Would you agree that the conditions that had been set by the Office of the Prosecutor as laid down in this letter were relevant not only to the competencies and mandated of Mr. Dzikov as public prosecutor but also impacting on the competencies and mandate of other state authority? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which other state authorities?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will refer you perhaps to condition number 4, where you set as a condition that there shall no Macedonian special forces, MUP, or military involved in the exhumation process. I suppose that you would agree that this in effect would curtail the usual abilities or mandate of the security forces of the Macedonia republic. Do I agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. But I would also add that agreement was perhaps one of the most crucial ones, because had the security forces of Macedonian been involved in the operation, it was generally accepted by all parties, including the Macedonian authorities, that that might be a precursor to a future reaction and counteraction by all parties, resulting in violent action.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you must agree with me that Mr. Dzikov, prior to giving his agreement to the conditions set, must have consulted with other authorities considering the fact that the request you had made concerned their mandate as well. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that decisions made it somewhere in the Macedonian authorities to cooperate with the Tribunal, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you are you aware, as well, that the Ministry of Interior did not try to resist the conditions that were set in this letter of yours of the 20th of February. They agreed to all the conditions as well, is that correct, are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are aware perhaps of a proposal or an offer made by Mr. Boskoski to provide security for the operation exhumation which was turned down?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- I can't recall that directly myself. It is -- it is possible that took place. I can't affirm or deny it sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated, yesterday, already that you were provided with some assistance or some type of assistance by the Ministry of Interior in the form of support by the crime technique department of the Ministry of Interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Tribunal weren't supplied with it. It was agreed it was a Macedonian operation, and they used the crime scene technicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that the team of crime technicians included the head of this unit, Miroslav Percinkovski?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: An individual called Simon Dzidrovski, the head of the identification department. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: A person called Zivko Stanovksi, chief inspector for, what is known as, the development on the field?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that gentleman's name. He may well have been there, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And other individuals who were ballistic or identification experts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Your Honours, if I may say, if may help, in my terminology, it would have been the complete scenes of crime package you would expect in any major crime investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you explain for the benefit of the Trial Chamber what part the crime technicians section of the Minister of Interior played in the exhumation an autopsy process.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crime technicians supplied personnel who would be present at both the exhumations and the autopsies, to photograph and record the proceedings, and to retain certain artifacts from the pathologists during the exhumation process such as clothing and that type of material.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did they assist as well with the examination of the clothing of the victims? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And they prepared sketches in preparation for the exhumation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I suppose you were satisfied with the work done by the crime technicians during that operation; is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were very professional in everything they did, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that agreeable to you, Mr. Tucker, that all through the year 2001 your office, the Office of the Prosecutor, expressed its satisfaction with the competent Macedonian authorities which assisted in the Ljuboten matter. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 2001? I'm not sure about 2001; but, to my knowledge, yes, for 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in 2002, a number of, let's say, letters of appreciation were sent back and forth between the Prosecution, the Office of the Prosecutor, and the competent Macedonian authority; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, but it certainly would not surprise me if that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, at this stage, I will ask you to turn to tab 24 of your binder. This is again Exhibit P391, and I will ask you to turn to what is annex B in -- annex C, I apologise, in the filing of the Prosecution. This would be N000-9883-17.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Briefly, on this letter, Mr. Tucker, you will agree that this is a letter signed and sent by Madam Del Ponte on the 14th of May of 2002 to Mr. Dzikov, the state prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply, if I can ask you it turn to the second page and draw your attention to last negligence of that letter, it says: "In conclusion, I wish to express my appreciation for your assistance in these cases." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I also ask you to turn to the next tab in your binder, that's tab 25. This is Rule 65 ter 1D624, and this is a letter of Mr. Patrick Lopez-Terres - we will come back to it - directed to Judge Nikolovski; and if I can ask you to turn to the last page of this document, the second page. Judge Nikolovski is, again, thanked by Mr. Lopez-Terres in those terms: "I take the opportunity of this letter to thank you for your cooperation you have already provided to our office and for the assistance we may request from you in the future." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yesterday, we discussed the fact that you took part in a number of meetings with the Macedonian authorities. We've seen that a number of those meetings related to the Neprosteno investigation, that the meetings in March and April of 2002 related to the Ljuboten investigation, and we have also seen that you had a number of meetings at the end of November of 2001 which related to both Neprosteno and Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that you had eight such meetings over three day: The 27th of November, the 28th of November, and the 29th of November. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the numbers. I'm sure you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply for the record, this would be tab 27 to tab 34. Those are the investigator's notes prepared by Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And for each of those meetings, Mr. Tucker, I understand that you would prepare an investigator's note which is essentially a summary of the discussions that take place during those meetings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that all of the meetings, and I'm talking of the meetings of the 27, 28, 29 of November, were arranged by your colleague, Mr. Szydlik of the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that is Mr. Szydlik, I suppose in coordination with your office, would decide whom to meet during those meetings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand. Whom to meet during the meetings?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, who to invite to each particular meeting, the lists of guests.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From my recollection, unless it was specifically with, for example, the Department of Justice, the larger meetings that I attended, if I recall correctly, were called by Mr. Boskoski as the Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, I will ask you to look at -- well, I'll ask you a follow-up on that. The meeting you've just mentioned was in relation to the Neprosteno investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can look at tab 27, for instance, of your binder, that's Exhibit 1D35?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look simply at the purpose header of this investigator's note, it says that the meeting were arranged by Mr. Szydlik for the visit of Dennis Milner. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. I can see from the participants there, this would be most likely a meeting that we, the Office of the Prosecutor, instigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would be the case of each and every one of the other seven meetings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without looking at them and the participants, I would be reluctant to answer "yes" or "no" to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if you can turn to tab 28, again, meeting arranged by Andrzej Szydlik for the visit of Dennis Milner. It is--

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can turn to tab 29, it is, again, meeting arranged by Andrzej Szydlik for the visit of Dennis Milner, 27 November 2001.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can turn to tab 30, meeting arranged by Andrzej Szydlik for the visit of Dennis Milner, 28 November 2001?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can to tab 31, it is a meeting arranged by Andrzej Szydlik for the visit of Dennis Milner, 28 November 2001?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can turn to tab 32, it is a meeting arranged by Andrzej Szydlik for the visit of Dennis Milner, 29 November 2001?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can to tab 33, it is a meeting arranged by Andrzej Szydlik for the visit of Dennis Milner, again, 29 November 2001?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Again, tab 34, it's a meeting arranged by Andrzej Szydlik for the visit of Dennis Milner, 29 November 2001.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that Mr. Boskoski was invited at none of those eight meetings? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also contract that at none of those meeting were members of the security forces invited to attend?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Going back for a moment, Mr. Tucker, to these meetings, in particular one meeting which I will point to you in a second. Is that correct that during one of these meetings, at which you were present, Mr. Milner made it clear that he, as a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, regarding the Macedonian judicial authorities as competent for the local investigation in Macedonia? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will draw your attention to this particular meeting. It is under tab 28 of your binder. It is Exhibit 1D195, MFI. This is a document that we have gone through, Mr. Tucker, and I will ask you simply to focus on a paragraph in the middle of the first page, which says this: "Dennis Milner explained that he would speak with the judiciary responsible for the Ljuboten investigation in order to establish what inquiries had been conducted to date and any result that resulted from those inquiries." Can you recall making that record?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it also correct that, during the same set of meetings, it was the view taken by the Office of the Prosecutor that it should not interfere with this judicial investigation? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask you to turn to the next nab your binder, tab 29, which is MFI, as 1D198. And, again, this is a document that we have seen already, but I will ask you to look at the second paragraph on that page, where Dennis Milner introduced representatives of the ICTY to the public prosecutor. He stated the reason -- the reason for his visit was a follow-up to that of the Prosecutor. He stressed the view of the Prosecutor that Macedonia was a sovereign state and had the responsibility and the capability to investigate crimes of this nature. He stated that it was not within the mandate of the Tribunal to interfere with that judicial processes. Do you recall making that note?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you sought assurances from the Macedonian authorities that they would investigate the matter of Ljuboten fairly and correctly, you sought those assurances from the judicial authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in particular, you sought those assurances from the Ministry of Justice; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, I am sorry to go back and forth, Mr. Tucker, but if I can ask you to go back to tab 28 of your binder, which is 1D195, MFI.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll ask you to look at the third paragraph on the first page, where a statement attributed to Mr. Milner read as follows: "Dennis Milner continued by stating that he will prepare a report for the Prosecutor on his return to The Hague. He was seeking assurances from the Macedonian authorities that with each of the cases, Neprosteno and Ljuboten, the investigations are being treated with the same objectivity." Can you recall making that note?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the list of participants up on the page, this would be the Minister of the Justice and his assistant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree, I suppose, that the Chief Prosecutor, as a lawyer of the civilian law tradition, would be quite familiar with the fact that the person in charge of an investigation is the investigative judge. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really not in a position to answer for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if I can you to look at tab 24, please, of your binder, this is, again, the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is Exhibit P381, Your Honour. This is the Prosecutor's request for deferral of the case -- of the cases, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, I'll kindly ask you to turn what is the fourth page of the document, but the third page of the filing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: For the registry's benefit, this would be N000-9883-04.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the Prosecutor said the following: "During a visit to Macedonia on 8 May 2002, the Prosecutor met with the Macedonian authorities and informed them that she had decided to assume primacy over the three investigation about which the Macedonian authorities had provided information, in addition to the two investigations -- in addition about which -- over the three investigation about which the Macedonian authorities had provided information, in addition to the two investigation that she had commenced on 9 November of 2001." And I'll ask you to turn now to tab 19 of this binder.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be 1D191. This is, again, the letter of agreement, Mr. Tucker; and if I can ask you to look at paragraph or point 1, condition 1 of letter, where Mr. Lopez-Terres says: "The authorities of the Republic of Macedonia agreed to undertake an exhumation of ten marked and identified graves situated in a graveyard at Ljuboten and acknowledge that the full judicial investigation in relation to the cause of death of the human remains interred at this location has commenced." You will agree that what Mr. Lopez-Terres was referring to was, in fact, a judicial investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the understanding of the Prosecution at the time of Madam Del Ponte's exercising what she believed to be the primacy that she could trigger was that the judicial authority was in charge of the investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Forgive me, I'm not sure I understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, are you aware of the fact that at the time, when Madam Del Ponte decided to exercise the primacy of the Tribunal on the 8th of May 2002, the understanding of your office was that a judicial authority was in charge and competent for the investigation of Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time of the -- that Madam Prosecutor exercised her primacy?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we could look at tab 25 of your binder, please, Mr. Tucker, that's Rule 65 ter 1D624. Can you agree that this is a letter signed by Patrick Lopez-Terres, chief of investigations; that it is sent to Judge Nikolovski; and that is dated 22nd of May of 2002? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that Mr. Nikolovski at the time was the investigative judge in charge of the Ljuboten investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to go through this letter with you. It says this: "Dear Judge Nikolovski, I refer to the visit of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, ICTY, to the Republic of Macedonia on the 8th of May 2002. During this visit, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal, Madam Del Ponte, met, amongst others, Prime Minister Ljupco Georgievski; the foreign minister, Mr. Casule; and the public prosecutor, Mr. Dzikov." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Mr. Lopez-Terres continues: "She informed the authorities of the Republic of Macedonia that she had decided to exercise its primacy, pursuant to Article 9 of the Statute of the Tribunal, over the national courts of the Republic of Macedonia in relation to five cases currently under investigation in your country." And there you would agree that two of those five case, Mr. Tucker, were Ljuboten and Neprosteno; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And will Lopez-Terres continues: "One of these case is the Ljuboten investigation which was assigned to you till now. The Prosecutor of the ICTY has confirmed in writing the decision, a copy of which was sent to public prosecutor Mr. Dzikov, dated 14 May 2002. In view of the decision of Madam Del Ponte to exercise the primacy of the Tribunal in this matter, it is anticipated that all further investigations into these five matters will seize; however, that will not include current inquiries that are in progress in relation to this investigation, for instance, in respect of the Ljuboten investigation, the forensic analysis, and subsequent reports, the autopsy reports on the identity of the deceased and the cause of death," et cetera. Were you aware of that particular letter, Mr. Tucker?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D201, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Tucker, that, in the course of your investigation, or in the course of your meetings with the Macedonian authorities in 2001 and 2002, you also had the opportunity to meet with representatives of the OSCE? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in the course of those meetings, the OSCE also made it clear to you that their understanding of what was going on in the country, Macedonia, was that the judicial authorities were in charge of the Ljuboten investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that specifically, but that is quite likely to have been the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall, perhaps, that they pointed out to you the difficulties which the Macedonian authorities had in investigating this and other similar cases? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you also recall that, during one of those meetings, the OSCE made it clear to you that they believed you, the Office of the Prosecutor, should provide assistance to the competent judicial authorities. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I can. I can't remember exactly in that context, but I recall the general conversation, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask to you turn to tab 27 of your binder, Mr. Tucker, this is, again, an investigator's note. It's already an exhibit as 1D35. If we briefly go through it, Mr. Tucker, this is, again, the same type of meeting. The date is 27 November 2001. The time is 9.45. Office of the OSCE, and there is a number of representative of the OSCE: Yourself, Mr. Milner, and Mr. Szydlik. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the meeting, as you can see from the second paragraph in the text, had to do with both Neprosteno and Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: At this stage, I will simply ask you to turn to the last page of this document and focus, please, on a paragraph which starts with the words "SM," which would be Sandra Mitchell, senior member of the OSCE. She said: "Sandra Mitchell, again, stated the importance, in her view, of ICTY involvement in the judicial process. She suggested the possibility of the ICTY providing guidance and/or advice to the Macedonian judicial authorities, on the review, preparation, and subsequent prosecution of suspects within the jurisdiction of the authorities." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in response to that, Mr. Milner said that: "He preferred to think of an open cooperation between the Macedonian judiciary and the ICTY lawyers." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the OSCE made no mention or no suggestion to the effect that you should provide assistance or guidance or advice to anyone other than the Macedonian judicial authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not according to this report, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you also aware of the fact, Mr. Tucker, that the European Committee for the Prevention of Torture and Inhumane Treatment took an interest in the Ljuboten incident, in particular as regard allegations of police mistreatment in police stations? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the specifics of the organisation, but I know there was a lot of international interest in this particular topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that like the OSCE had done, as we have just seen, the European Committee Against Torture took the view that the authorities which were competent in Macedonia to investigation allegations of police brutalities in police stations were again the judicial authorities? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps, I will kindly ask you to turn to tab 35 of your binder. This has been MFI'd as P380. This is a report to the government of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia dated 16 January 2003. And I will ask to you turn to the third page of that document, Mr. Tucker. This is the part of the report which relates to the Ljuboten incident. The actual report is larger in size.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask the registry to turn to ERN N001-4771, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can look at what numbered paragraph 27, I will read the first two sentences to you. It says that: "The CPT delegation examined a series of cases of alleged ill-treatment emerging in the aftermath of an operation by government security forces in the village of Ljuboten near Skopje on 10 to 12 August 2001. The delegation focussed its attention on the treatment of those persons who had been deprived of their liberty by the police in the course or after the Ljuboten operation." So you would agree that this appears to be the allegations of police brutalities which followed the operation during the weekend of the 10 to 12th August 2001? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to turn to the next page, please, I will ask to you look at the second paragraph within --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly ask the counsel to speak a little bit slower.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, yet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask you to look at the second paragraph of paragraph 28, the Committee makes the following comment: "In this connection, it should be noticed that the response by the Ministry of Justice to the delegations immediate observations under Article 8, paragraph 5 for the Convention relayed the following statement from Basic Court II. The Court underlines that there has been no decision in respect of instituting court procedure against maltreatment by the law enforcement organs. "Given that the information set out in the preceding subparagraph can be said to amount to prima facie, evidence that that ill-treatment may have occurred, the CPT would like to be informed of the reasons for the absence of the decision to institute the court procedure against maltreatment, as well as to receive the views of the relevant public prosecutor on this matter." And if you can now turn to the second paragraph of paragraph 29, it says this: "For its part, the Ministry of Justice has also informed the CPT by the letter of 14 February 2002 that it is in the process of establishing an independent expert body to examine the allegations for possible cases of torture after the events in Ljuboten and to prepare a report, a copy of which is it to be submitted to the CPT. The CPT welcomes this undertaking and looks forward to receiving a copy of that report in the near future." At this point, Mr. Tucker, would you agree that the CPT took the view that the relevant public prosecutor, as they call it, and the Ministry of Justice were responsible for this matter, and that the Ministry of Justice responded that it would act upon the request made by the CPT? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to turn to what is numbered as page 23 of this report, this is N001-4775, and that would be the last paragraph before point 5. It says that: "By letter of 27 November 2001, addressed to the Minister of Foreign Affairs, the president of the CPT recalled the delegations request for certain information relating to the -- with the Atulla Qaili's case, including inter alia an account of any judicial action taken to investigate the manner in which he was treated by the law enforcement agencies, details of any decision concerning the initiation of court proceedings related to ill-treatment by the law enforcement agencies and the information on which a decision to proceed or not to proceed was based." And, again, you will agree that the CPT had taken the view that the matter pertaining to the AQ case was a judicial matter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The court reporter has requested the counsel to speak slower please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We have just become aware of that fact, and we are giving them a breathing space.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, is it correct that, when you met with the judicial authorities in -- at the end of November of 2001, they told you, in no uncertain terms, that they were competent to investigate the matter of Ljuboten and never suggested that you should go and talk to someone else about this matter? Is it correct.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, we'll look at the material then -- we'll look first, perhaps, at the Neprosteno matter, if we may. And for the assistance of the Chamber, perhaps, could you explain in a short summary what the Neprosteno case is all about?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this particular case involved the disappearance, the alleged abduction, of a number of Macedonian civilians by the organisation known as the NLA, where it was believed that they had been, once abducted, subject to torture and subsequent murder, and the bodies buried in undisclosed locations in the area of Neprosteno.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, there is a more complete information concerning the Neprosteno incident in the document which is under tab 8 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, I'd kindly ask you to turn to tab 30, 3-0, of your binder, please. This would be Rule 65 ter 1D657. It has an ERN 1D00-5880. If we can go through this document together, Mr. Tucker, this is one of the meetings we have seen arranged by your colleague, Mr. Szydlik, for the visit of Mr. Milner. The date is 28 November 2001. The time is 9.40 in the morning. The location is the Institute for Forensic Science in Skopje, and there is a long list of people present at this meeting, including Ms. Aleksandra Zajirovska, Mr. Milner, Mr. Szydlik, yourself, and your interpreter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall that, during these meeting, Ms. Zajirovska, who at the time was an investigative judge for the Tetovo regional court, was introduced to you as the person in charge of the Neprosteno investigation? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can turn to the second page of that document, please, that would be 1D00-5881. I'd like to draw your attention to the third paragraph on that page. It reads as follows: "Mr. Arifi, president of the Tetovo regional court, introduced himself and explained the procedure of the regional court system in Macedonia. He explained that he had appointed Madam Aleksandra Zajirovska as the investigating judge for the investigation, and Mr. Boris Mirosavlevski as the public prosecutor. "Madam Zajirovska was in charge of the investigation, reporting through the public prosecutor to himself. He stated that the evidence would be correlated by the investigative judge for the judicial court and possibly for the ICTY and will be assessed based on its merits. The evidence, as he understood the situation, would also be reviewed by the Tribunal." Does that correctly reflect what was told to you at the time by Mr. Arifi, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it does, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Moving on now to the Ljuboten investigation. Is that correct that Prosecutor Serafimovski, Deputy Prosecutor Dragan Cakic, and Investigative Judge Dragan Nikolovski were introduced to you as the organ or persons competent to investigate crimes in or around Ljuboten? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think my recollection was that they were only competent for the area of Neprosteno.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, I will ask you to turn to tab 31 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is MFI'd as 1D197.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is, again, a meeting organised by your office on the 28 November 2001. The time is 1320. It took place at the office of the higher public prosecutor in Skopje, and among those present were Gregor [sic] Serafimovski, who was acting higher public prosecutor; Mr. Dragoljub Cakic, deputy primary public prosecutor; Mr. Dragan Nikolovski, investigative judge at the primary court Skopje II; Jani Nica, criminal judge; Ljubomir Joleski, criminal judge; Maja Konevska, deputy public prosecutor; Mr. Milner; Szydlik; yourself; and your interpreter, Ms. Brajovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I apologise. I misunderstood the previous question. These are the individuals who were responsible for the [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I am grateful. It might have to do with my question. I'd kindly ask to you look at the second paragraph on this page, which starts with the words "Mr. Serafimovski": "Mr. Serafimovski, acting higher public prosecutor, welcomed the ICTY to the meeting and thanked them for attending. He identified the other members of department to Dennis Milner." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then there's a paragraph that pertains to Neprosteno, and then it says: "He spoke of the difficulties involved in both investigations, and the danger to those investigating the issues and those supplying the information. He also referred to the media release of information that also added to the difficulties and an increase in tension within the communities affected by the exhumation. He also referred to previous attacks by NLA members." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask you to turn to the next page, that would be 1D00-5531. Mr. Serafimovski continues: "Mr. Serafimovski then spoke about Ljuboten and the practical difficulties that faced the investigation team, security problems, and an inability to visit the scene of the killings as well as the grave sites. He also spoke of the official version of the events of the day of the incident. "He said that five members of the KLA had been killed at the scene and were laying in the field where they fell; however, on site investigation was impossible due to security considerations. They received information that the deceased were buried the following day. He explained the judicial process and the appointment of an investigative judge to take charge of the investigation." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if you can go a little bit further in the document, there is a passage which refers to a Mr. Sokic, which should we believe be "Mr. Cakic," deputy primary public prosecutor, explained his roll to you. He said: "He stated that the investigation in to Ljuboten had already been opened despite the lack of information necessary to do so. They had been waiting for the information from the Ministry of Interior for sometime. However, he did say that he had been in contact with Professor Duma at the Institute of Forensic Science Skopje." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then Mr. Cakic -- you record them as saying: "They had not been able to visit the scene of the killings to conduct an on-site investigation or visit the site of the graves of the victims. No interviews had been conducted with the relatives of the victims or any other investigation with other potential witnesses (security concerns). He emphasised that he and his colleagues were willing to commence the investigation as soon as the situation permits, but he was not prepared to go to the area until the security issues had been resolved. Mr. Cakic explained that he had already experience of being 'blown up' during such an exercise and considered himself fortunate to have survived." And I think, Mr. Tucker, you have already indicated that those security concerns were expressed by the relevant Macedonian authorities whom you met; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph, Mr. Milner says this: "Dennis Milner reassured all present that it was not the intention of the ICTY to commence until the security concerns had been addressed. He then explained the role of the ICTY in the investigations and the sovereign right and duty of Macedonia to investigate all matters of this nature that are presented to them. "He also assured those present that the Prosecutor, ICTY, had no intention to put pressure or to attempt to influence Macedonia in their investigation." Then Mr. Serafimovski says that: "Mr. Serafimovski stated that the involvement of the ICTY was critical to the investigations in order to dispel false rumours in the media and from other sources." Can you recall Mr. Serafimovski making that point?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you met with Mr. Serafimovski, on this occasion but also perhaps on other occasions, he made it clear and evident to you that he considered himself and the other judicial authorities as competent to investigate Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And my recollections are connect now. It was dependent, of course, on the security situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he never suggested to that you should go and talk to someone else in relation to this investigation; is that correct? He was the man in charge.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about another matter, if you can recall it or if you have any knowledge of it. Can you recall during any of your meetings with the Macedonian authorities that they explained to until that time, when the Office of the Prosecutor had made a formal request for deferral of the case to its jurisdiction, they were required to continue with their investigation? Do you recall the judicial authorities telling you that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not precisely in those terms. I can't remember the exact details no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, I will ask you, again, to look at tab 24 of your binder. This is, again, Exhibit P391, and I'll ask to turn, again, to annex H of this document. This would be N000-9883-38. Mr. Tucker, this is letter which we have already seen very briefly in relation to other particular point, and we will come back to it. But at this stage, I will simply ask you to identify the letter. Again, this is a letter of the public prosecutor office of Macedonia. It is dated the 2nd of September of 2002, and it is sent to Madam Del Ponte, Chief Prosecutor of the ICTY, OTP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, and annex H that you have referred to me is actually dated the 2nd of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. If I can ask you to turn to the second page of that document, in the fourth full paragraph of this page, Mr. Dzikov says the following, it is the middle of the paragraph: "The public prosecutor's office and the courts are legally obliged to continue with the investigative and criminal proceedings before the competent domestic Courts because it is a case of person being prosecuted as responsible for serious violations of the international human right law to whom the Law on Amnesty cannot be applied, nor do [sic] this crime expire." So you will agree that Mr. Dzikov, in any case, took the view that the judicial authorities had an obligation to continue until the time when the primacy of the Tribunal was triggered. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the first sentence of the next paragraph, you will agree that, again, the Prosecutor took the view that the investigation into those five cases, which were the subject of deferral discussions, were within the competence of the public prosecutor and the court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that this is a view that the state prosecutor or the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia, again, reiterated during the deferral hearing in this matter before this Tribunal? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sir. I wasn't party to those proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd kindly ask you to turn to tab 26 of your binder. This is Rule 65 ter 1D638.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could turn to what is the end of page 14 of the transcript, please. That would be the previous page, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you could look at the last sentence, starting before the indication page 14, please, Mr. Tucker, I will read it for you. It says this: "The public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia, senior public prosecutor, and the basic public prosecutors, in accordance with their constitutional function of criminal prosecution of perpetrators of criminal acts, among which are the evil doing acts of severe criminal offences of violations of the international humanitarian law on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia, and according also to the international rules and regulations, undertook activities for collection of evidence against the organisers, leaders, conspirers, and other perpetrators." And then there is a sentence which says: "Before the competent Macedonia courts, ongoing are the procedures. So you will agree, Mr. Tucker, that, again, Mr. Dzikov -- those terms of those of Mr. Dzikov indicated that they, the judicial authority and himself in particular, were in charge of this ongoing procedure, is that correct, as far as the Macedonian authorities are concerned, in any case?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to turn a little bit further, at page 18 of the transcript, please, were you aware of the fact that Mr. Dzikov at the time had indicated that, unless the Office of the Prosecutor would seize itself of the matter, the Macedonian authorities would then be required to, let's say, reactivate their investigation? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, perhaps, I'll ask you to look at the record of the hearing again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could scroll down -- a little bit further down the page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will draw your attention to the sentence which starts with the words: "But in case." Can you locate it. It is towards the end of the page.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Has it got a line number, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would be line 12?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, I have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, this is, as you can see from further up in the page, submissions made by Mr. Dzikov, the state prosecutor. He says that: "But in case that the Prosecution within The Hague Tribunal or The Hague Tribunal decide not to defer the five cases, then, according to Article 9, paragraph 1 from the Statute of the Tribunal, Macedonian judicial institutions, the public prosecutor, and the courts have the legal opportunity and obligation to continue further the very investigative procedures and the criminal procedures before the competent national court," and then if you turn, "because it is criminal prosecution of perpetrators responsible for severe invitations of the international humanitarian law, perpetrators to which the Law on Amnesty cannot be applied, and the crimes themselves are not subject to exceeding statute of limitation." So does that correspond to your memory of the information which were given to you by the Macedonian authorities which you met?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't remember who gave me the information, but I can certainly remember the content, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, I will also draw the Chamber's attention to paragraph 43 of decision on deferral of the Trial Chamber of 4 October 2002. This is in tab 37 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as was seen from various passages that I have read to you in the last half-hour or so, you would agreed that the Macedonian authorities investigation was ongoing at the time? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you knew that an investigation had been open, that a judge and prosecutor were in charge of the matter at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you also aware that at some point in the late summer and early Autumn of 2001, after the events of Ljuboten, a number of meetings had been organised between members of the Ministry of Interior and members of the Forensic Institute? Were you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is before my arrival in November, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will simply refer to the evidence of Dr. Jakovski on those point of view of the response of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply to clarify, Mr. Tucker, I don't want to redo the point too much, but you were aware, up until at least the 25th of September of 2002, and that's the time of the deferral hearing, that, until that point, the Macedonian authorities -- the competent Macedonian authorities had been conducted an investigation and that investigation was ongoing? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you also aware that one of the reasons why the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal requested the matter to be deferred to your competencies or the competencies of the Office of the Prosecutor was a risk of collusion, to use the term, between the two parallel investigations, yours and the investigation conducted by the Macedonian authorities? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of what -- what decision was taken by the Prosecutor as to why she would exercise primacy at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, I'll just ask you, in that case, to go back, once again, to tab 24 of this binder. This is, again, the Prosecution request for deferral. It is Exhibit P391. Mr. Tucker, I'll ask you to turn to paragraph 13, 1-3, of this Prosecution filing, and the submissions that were made by the Prosecution in this filing read as follows: "There is no doubt that the ongoing Macedonian investigations and Prosecution into crimes allegedly committed by NLA members in 2001 are closely related to the Prosecutor's investigations of the same acts. Similarly any investigations and Prosecution concerning the activities of the Macedonian forces against Macedonian Albanian civilians in Macedonia during 2001, including the alleged crimes committed in Ljuboten, are also closely related to the Prosecutor's investigations of the same acts." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph, paragraph 14, the Prosecution or the Office of the Prosecutor said this: "Parallel investigations of the same criminal acts by the Prosecutor and the Macedonian authorities will likely jeopardise the Prosecutor's ability to resolve her investigation in a successful manner. The Macedonian authorities will inevitably interview witnesses that the Prosecutor seeks to interview. "Multiple interviews of witnesses by different authorities risks to produce conflicting statements, confused lines of inquiry, and antagonise witnesses. In addition, the Macedonian authorities will likely seek to seize and analyse physical and forensic evidence which would compromise the Prosecutor's ability to analyse the same evidence. "Finally, to the extent that the Macedonian authorities rely on investigative procedure, techniques, and strategies that are different from those relied upon by the Prosecutor, their acts could compromise or taint subsequent investigative efforts by the Prosecutor. "In short, the Prosecutor submits that the continued investigations and prosecutions by the Macedonian authorities into the same acts being investigated by the Prosecution will have serious implementations for the Prosecutor's investigations." So would you agree that at least one of the reason advanced by the Prosecution, your office, the Office of the Prosecutor, for the deferral of cases was the risk of collusion between the two investigations? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, this particular argument of the Prosecution was taken into conversation by the Trial Chamber; again, its decision and deferral at paragraph 11, which summarized the submissions of the Prosecutor, and paragraph 12 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, are you aware that, once the Trial Chamber of this Tribunal had rendered its decision on the deferral of these five cases to the jurisdiction of this Tribunal, the Macedonian authorities then proceeded with the actual transfer of those cases? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree, I hope, that the authorities which deferred to the jurisdiction of the Tribunal were neither the Ministry of Interior or even the government of Macedonia, but the courts competent with these matters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those would be the basic local courts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my understanding, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to turn to tab 38A of your binder, please?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry which tab, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would be, well, tab 38, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. This would be Rule 65 ter 1D664. It is ERN 1D00-5908; and in the Macedonian version, it would be 1D00-5904.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an unofficial translation of the document. If admitted, we would submit it to the CLSS for an official translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, if you can look first at the top left-hand corner of that document, you will see that it comes from the Supreme Court of the Republic of Macedonia, and the date of this document called "Conclusions" is 6 November 2002. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look immediately at the second paragraph of that document, and more specifically at the sentence, which is the sixth line from the bottom, it starts with the word: "At the question of counsel." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the Supreme Court of Macedonia said the following: "At the question of the counsel, the state public prosecutor also confirmed that Republic of Macedonia will not object to the taking over of the two investigations considered; namely, the investigations Neprosteno and Ljuboten. With regard to these investigations, the alleged perpetrator were still unknown. To support his suggestions, he claimed that there still exists reasonable fear that the security situation in Macedonia and the place that was established recently could be interrupted if this case are to be hand by domestic courts." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then, to save time, we will you go through the document and to the third paragraph in paragraph number 4 in this document, where it says: "Therefore, it is the obligation." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The decision reads: "Therefore, it is the obligation of the basic courts that acted on the mentioned cases to respect the formal request of the International Court according to the deadline determined in Article 11 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the International Court. And then at paragraph 5, the Supreme Court says: "The basic courts, depending on what phase the procedures are in, investigation, indictment, main trial, possible judgement, will do the transfer pursuant to the established authorities -- authority by the Law on Criminal Procedure." So, Mr. Tucker, does that record with your own memory of the competence of the authorities which had to defer the case back to you or to you?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You indicated already that you met with our client, Mr. Boskoski, on a number of occasions. Can you recall from any of those particular meeting where Mr. Boskoski made it clear to you that his own understanding of the situation was that it was the judicial authorities, in particular the prosecutor, who was in charge of the investigation at Ljuboten? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Tucker, I would kindly ask you to look at a short video-clip. This was a video that was provided to us by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The transcript is under tab 39 of your binder, Your Honour, and this is Rule 65 ter 1D684.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Armed groups are blocking the peaceful integration process. This is one thing that I'm sure of, that the Macedonian security forces have the strength, the preparedness to return the constitutional order. At this moment, all the arguments have been exhausted. All of the arguments are in the side of the Republic of Macedonia, and all of the arguments are in our hands. Europe and the international community significantly changes their position about the Republic of Macedonia, and I think that we have a great advantage. I think we are ready that we change every problem according to the constitutional set up of Macedonia. "According to the case of Ljuboten. Minister Boskoski responded: 'There are no dilemmas about that question. We, the Macedonian police, were the first ones who asked for investigation to be carried out on the location. And if you bring back your memory, you will remember that well that we did not conduct this investigation because the armed groups on the village of Ljuboten did not allow the investigative judge, the criminalistic police and the three independent institutions to enter the village and verify the factual situation the same day that killings were reported which could have resolved that matter.'" "Boskoski, when asked if MVR had sent a list of individuals who had committed war crimes to The Hague Tribunal: 'We respect the International Court, and we will do everything necessary to submit the crimes that occurred in the Republic of Macedonia. And to this end, we have submitted evidence. You know that the criminal charges were brought against approximately 20 individuals for serious crimes, crimes which are prosecuted in accordance with international law, crimes which are within the jurisdiction of The Hague Tribunal. So, of course, we will cooperate.'" "What about the disagreement with public prosecutor Stavre Dzikov? He had a meeting with the representatives of The Hague Tribunal as early as the 20th and most probably authorised work to take place in Ljuboten. Were you not aware of that?" "Look, whatever the public prosecutor greed to, that is a separate and independent institution, and I have no intention of getting involved in his affairs. I know what my responsibilities are, and I intend to finish them in the way that I started."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just for clarification, Your Honour, I'm wondering if my learned colleague could tell us approximately when this video was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we have received the document from the Prosecutor, and we have not been able to put a certain date on the video itself. But if it is an issue relevant to the Prosecutor, I'm sure we can figure out with them. In any case, at this stage, we would seek to tender this document, Your Honour, and the transcript, which is under tab 39.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Tab 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Tab 39, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The video and transcript will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps before the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D102, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps before the break, Mr. Tucker, were you aware of that particular video-clip? Have you ever seen it?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure it would be, Mr. Mettraux. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, you will recall in the video that I have just shown to you, the interview of Mr. Boskoski, that he indicated in the video that the Ministry of Interior had been the first to ask for an investigation in the village of Ljuboten. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall Mr. Boskoski saying that in the video, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the course of your investigation, or in the course of your meetings with various authorities, did you have an opportunity to verify that claim or at least what you now to be the claim of Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I ask you to turn to tab 24 of your binder once again, Mr. Tucker. This is, again, the Prosecutor's request for deferral.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And for the registry's assistance, this is P391, and the ERN in question would be N000-9883-51.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, if you can work with the same guidance, it would be, again, this page 61 on the top right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this is the same material provided by the Macedonian authorities about case Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask you to look at the middle of the first paragraph, in the section case Ljuboten, there's a sentence starting with the word: "On August 142001, at 12.55." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will just read out for the transcript. It says: "On August 14, 2001, at 1255 hours, the Ministry of Interior informed the deputy public prosecutor and the investigative judge that there are five dead bodies in the village the Ljuboten. The Ministry immediately informed an expert team composed of the proposed -- the magistrate judge of the Principal Court Skopje II, Skopje; principal public prosecutor; and experts from the Ministry of Interior to examine the site. Mr. Tucker, would you agree that this, in fact, supports the comment made by Mr. Boskoski in the video which we've seen a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it appears so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Tucker, I will have another binder given to you, to Your Honours, and to the Prosecutor with another set of documents. Mr. Tucker, in the course of your work in relation to this case, or more generally in relation to the Macedonian situation, did you become aware of public calls made by Mr. Boskoski to the effect that an exhumation and an autopsy should take place in the village of Ljuboten? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask you to turn to tab 40 of your binder, second binder, that would be the first document. This is Rule 65 ter 130. As you can see, this is a press report with a title, "Interior Minister Boskoski expresses satisfaction with OSCE attitude," and it is dated 15 August, 2001. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask to you look at one of the last paragraph on this document, starting with the words: "About the affair in Ljuboten." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the report say this is: "About the affair in Ljuboten, Boskoski informed that by the time the expert team had arrived on site, the bodies were already buried." Then there is a quote attributed to him: "In order to know truth, an exhumation acknowledged by the Prosecutor will have to take place, he explained." Mr. Tucker, were you aware of this call by Mr. Boskoski for an exhumation?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D203, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You have heard also, I think, in the video that was shown to you a moment ago, that Mr. Boskoski undertook to assist and support the work of the Tribunal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will recall, I hope, that shortly after the events at Ljuboten, Mr. Boskoski also set up a commission to look into the events of Ljuboten. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware that -- well, are you aware of the existence of a report prepared by the commission set up by Mr. Boskoski to look into the events at Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware at the time, but I am aware now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, perhaps, that following the issuance of this report, the president or the head of this particular commission, Mr. Mitevski, recommended that an exhumation and an autopsy should take place in relation to Ljuboten? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at the time. I am now.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, perhaps, I will show you the document, which may assist later. It is under tab 41A of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your honour, this is already admitted. It is exhibit, Exhibit 1D33.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, if you look at the top left-hand corner of the document, it says that it the comes from the Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior, office of public security. It is dated the 7th of September, 2001. It is sent to the public prosecutor's office and the duty investigating judge of Lower Court Skopje II, and the title of this document is "Motion" or "Recommendation," in another translation, "for exhumation an autopsy." Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to turn to the third and last page of that document in the English, which would be N000-7334-ET, you will agree that the document in question was signed by Director Goran Mitevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is -- in the English translation, it indicates that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you can look, if you wish, at the Macedonian version of it on the last page, to see that there is a signature there. Is that correct?
