utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to look at the last paragraph on that document, there is a recommendation that is made and reads as follows: "Due to the aforementioned, we believe that the motion for exhumation and autopsy is justified and should be accepted, with the aim of identifying the five corpses and establishing the cause of death of the five individuals from the village Ljuboten." Does that correspond to your memory of what was requested by Mr. Mitevski at the time and by the Ministry of Interior in general?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was certainly not aware of this at the time; but, later, I was aware of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were you aware at the time of the call made by Mr. Mitevski for this particular exhumation and autopsy?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware, perhaps, that this particular call made by Mr. Mitevski for an exhumation and autopsy had been made at the behest of Mr. Boskoski himself?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I ask you it turn to tab 41 of your binder. It is Exhibit 1D34. As you can see from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps, I should assist the registry. There's also a Macedonian version of this document, 1D34.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can look at the cover page of that document, you can see that it comes from the Ministry of Interior. It is dated November 2001, and it is some information about the events in the vicinity of the Skopje village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to turn to the last page in the English of this document?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd ask you to focus on the last paragraph, and I will read it out to you. It says this: "Having in consideration the importance of the exhumation as the investigative act, in order to resolve the reasons for the death, the Minister of the Interior, Ljube Boskoski, immediately after the case, has submitted the written recommendation to the principal public prosecutor office, Skopje II, in Skopje to start conducting the process of exhumation of the corpse of the people, in order to continue with post-mortem and thorough examination." Mr. Tucker, you would agree that this statement refers to the document that I have shown to you a moment ago, or appears, in any case, to refer to that document?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly appears to, because I can't authenticate these documents..

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree also that on the basis of this particular document Mr. Boskoski appears to have been the person on whose behest the request or the recommendation was made; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would certainly be indicated by this document, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Are aware also, Mr. Tucker, that the Ministry of Interior had immediately notified the competent investigative judge, Mr. Nikolovski, that an operation had been taken place in Ljuboten and that a recommendation was made to him for an autopsy and an exhumation? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then I'll ask to you look at tab 64 of your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is, again, already an exhibit. This is 1D73.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll just you go through this document with you quickly, Mr. Tucker. As you can see, this is coming from the Ministry of Interior, criminal police. This is an Official Note that is submitted by Simon Dzidrovski and Besim Ramicevic. It is dated the 18 of September of 2001, and it is dispatched to the director of MVR, Ministry of Interior, publicity security bureau, head of criminal police section, analytics an investigations sector, criminal technical sector, general crime sector. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look at the first paragraph of this Official Note, it says that: "On 14th September of 2001, a consultation meeting instigated by the investigative judge of Lower Court Skopje II, Dragan Nikolovski, was held in the premises of the Forensic Medicine and Criminology Institute in order to discuss the undertaking of measures, in accordance with Article 244 of the Law on Criminal Procedure for the exhumation and autopsy of individuals buried in the village of Ljuboten, who died during the military operations that took place in the area." Then, if you can pass over the next paragraph, which listed the persons present on that occasion, there's a paragraph which reads: "Mr. Nikolovski, the investigative judge, informs those present that MVR," that's the Ministry of Interior "had notified the public prosecutor's office in Skopje of the armed operation undertaken in the area of the village of Ljuboten by the security forces and had recommended the initiation of measures for the exhumation an autopsy of the casualties." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree that this document suggests that the Ministry of Interior had, in fact, informed the public prosecutor's office of the exists of an operation in the area after the operation, and had recommended the initiation of an exhumation an autopsy? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly suggests so in this document, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look at the next paragraph, it says: "In accordance with the notification, deputy public prosecutor, Dragoljub Cakic, dispatched the recommendation to the investigative judge, Nikolovski, who called for the meeting with the aim of reaching an agreement on the methods and means for the realisation of the investigation." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is also another document which I would wish to show you, Mr. Tucker. This is already an exhibit, Prosecution Exhibit P55.10, and you will find it under tab 83 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. If you look at this document, Mr. Tucker, this comes from the basic public prosecution office. It has a number, and it is date the 18th of March 2002. It is sent to Basic Court Skopje II, investigative judge, Mr. Dragan Nikolovski. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention to the first paragraph of that document, it says: "Regarding the initiative of the MOI-the directorate for public security number 10-33282, dated 7 September, 2001, to the title "XXRO number 109801," dated 10/09/2001, in accordance with Article 148, paragraph 1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, a proposal was submitted regarding undertaking certain investigation actions, exhumation from Article 244 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, so as to examine and perform prosection of the bodies of unknown persons buried at the local cemetery in the village of Ljuboten, determine their identity, cause of death, time of death, the circumstances under which the deaths occurred, since it was impossible to do so on the 13 and 14 August 2001, due to the known reasons, on-site investigation by the competent bodies was made impossible." Is that correct that the first part of that very long sentence, again, refers to the fact that the initiative for those measures came from the MOI, and more specifically the directorate for public security? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can turn to the next tab in your binder, this is, again, a Prosecution Exhibit. It is P55.13, 1-3. Mr. Tucker, you will agree this appears to be an Official Note regarding going on site in the village of Ljuboten, Skopje area. This is dated the 19th of March, of 2002, and it comes from the basic public prosecution office. And if I can draw your attention, again, to first to the first paragraph of that document, it reads as follow: "On 19 March 2002, upon proposal of the basic public prosecution office in Skopje, and in relation to the initiative of the MOI-directorate for public security, with number 1033282, dated 7 September 2001, and the proposal to the investigative judge of the Basic Court Skopje II, XXRO number 1098-01, dated 10 September 2001, on undertaking an investigative action, exhumation from Article 244 from the Criminal Code -- from the Code of Criminal Procedure, so as to examine and perform prosection of the bodies of the ten persons buried in the local cemetery in the village of Ljuboten in order to determine their identity, cause of death, time of death, and the circumstances under which death occurred, the investigative village judge went on site in the village of Ljuboten with the purpose of becoming directly familiar with the location and position of the buried persons, all this so as to perform the exhumation as successful as possible." Mr. Tucker, again, on the base of this document, you would agree, once again, that the initiative for these steps taken had come from the MOI-directorate for public security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I ask you turn, then, to the next tab in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is also an exhibit, 1D73. I'm sorry. We have reviewed this one. This is the next one that I would like to bring to your attention. I apologise to the registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is it tab 86 of your binder. This is part of Exhibit P55, and it has an ERN ET-N002-1148-9002-1148-1, and the Macedonian version of this document is N002-1146-003. Mr. Tucker, I'll go through this document briefly with you. As you can see from the title on the left-hand corner, or the sender in any case, it comes from the basic public prosecution office. It has the same number that we have seen several times before, 1098-01. It is dated the 10th of September of 2001, and it is addressed to the Basic Court Skopje II, to the attention of the investigative judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the title of the document is: "A proposal on undertaking certain investigative action." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the second paragraph of that document, I will read it out to you. It starts with the word: The public prosecution office": "The public prosecution office in relation to this case, acting pursuant to Article 148, paragraph 1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, and upon the written initiative of the MOI which has been handed to this title, during duty outside of regular working hours, on 7 September 2001, gives a proposal on undertaking certain investigation action; namely, as follows: In order to determine the identity of the five person buried on 14 August 2001 in the local cemetery in the village of Ljuboten, to determine the cause of death, time of death, and circumstances under which death occurred, and so as to perform an exhumation and prosection of their bodies to order the investigation, action exhumation, in accordance with Article 244 of the Code of Criminal Procedure." And, again, you will agree that this confirms the fact that the initiative for this investigative measures had come from the MOI. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the last paragraph of this document, it says: "The exhumations and afterwards the examination and prosection are to be assigned to the Institute of Forensic Medicine and Criminology with the medical faculty in Skopje." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is signed by deputy public prosecutor, Dragoljub Cakic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there's another document I would wish to show you. It is, again, a Prosecution Exhibit. It is under tab 90 of your binder. This is P55.11?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will draw, again, your attention to the top of the document on the left. This is, again, a document that comes from the basic prosecution office. It bears, again, the same number, 1098-01. It is dated 19/03/2002, and sent to Basic Court Skopje II, again, to the attention of Mr. Dragan Nikolovski. And I will draw attention, again, to the first paragraph. And, perhaps, to save time, I will ask to you look through it, because it is similar to the paragraph that I have read to you a number of times, and simply to ask you to confirm that, again, this document suggests that the MOI, and in particular the directorate for public prosecutor security, initiated the various investigative measures mentioned in that paragraph. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will also recall the view taken by Mr. Boskoski in the video that I have shown to you earlier on, that he understood that at this stage, at the time of the video in any case, the responsibility with the investigation was with the public prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We still don't know the date of the -- when this video was made that was shown to Mr. Tucker a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I have suggested no date, Your Honour, to the witness. I said at the time when the video was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, no. That's correct, but the question was phrased this way: "That Mr. Boskoski understood at this stage, at the time of the video in any case, the responsibility with the investigation was with the public prosecutor." But the problem that I see is, if we don't know when Mr. Boskoski made those statements that were recorded on the video, how --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But if those statements reveal a state of knowledge by Mr. Boskoski, isn't the question a proper one, even though we don't know the time? It remains an unsolved mystery, the time. But if the video shows Mr. Boskoski saying that Mr. Saxon is a nice man, isn't it fair to ask -- isn't it clear from the video that at that time Mr. Boskoski thought Mr. Saxon a nice man?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Agreed, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I haven't seen this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And Mr. Boskoski agrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I haven't seen this particular video, Your Honour, so I will stick with the other video.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, would you agree that at that time when Mr. Boskoski gave the interview, which you saw on your screen a moment ago, he expressed the view that at that time the person in charge of the investigation was the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd like to turn now to a somewhat different issue, Mr. Tucker, and that's a point that we have already touched upon on a number of occasion, but that is the issue of security, which I mentioned earlier. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall also that during your various meetings with the -- with different Macedonian authorities, they had indicated to you that they were concerned about certain risk and difficulties in their investigation. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall in particular that these concerns as to security and risks involved in the investigation related to, among other investigation, the Ljuboten investigation. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask to you go back, if you may, to your first binder, which is at your feet, I believe, and to turn to tab 31, Mr. Tucker. That would be Exhibit 1D197, MFI. Tab 31, Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd ask to you look at the last paragraph on that page. We have already seen it briefly earlier on. Those are statements or terms that were attributed to Mr. Serafimovski, the acting higher public prosecutor, and he said: "He spoke of the difficulties involved in both investigations and the danger of those investigating the issues and those supplying the information. He also referred to the media release of information that also added to the difficulties and an increase in tension within the communicates affected by the communication. He also referred to previous attacks by NLA members. Do you recall Mr. Serafimovski saying this?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can turn to the next page, this is, again, a comment that we have seen. But Mr. Serafimovski then spoke about Ljuboten, and he said: "The practical difficulties that faced the investigation team, security problems and an inability to visit the scene of the killings, as well as the grave sites. He also spoke of the official version of the events on the day of the incident. He said that five members of the KLA had been killed at the scene and were laying in a field where they fell. And he said: 'However, on site investigation was impossible due to security considerations. They received information that the deceased were buried the following day.' He explained the judicial process and the appointment of an investigative judge to take charge of the investigation." Again, Mr. Tucker, do you recall Mr. Serafimovski expressing those concerns and making those comments?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you recall also, I believe we have talked about that a moment ago, that the Macedonian authorities had expressed to you their readiness to continue with the investigation as soon as the security situation would permit. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this statement, as can be seen from this same note, was made by Mr. Cakic, the deputy primary public prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that same prosecutor explained to you that one of the reasons why he had particular security concern was that he had himself experienced being what he said "blown up" during such an exercise. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also the situation that later on in 2002, in March 2002, when you met again with the Macedonian authorities -- the competent Macedonian authorities, they, again, expressed their concern or security concerns to you in relation to the investigation in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall, in particular, the investigative judge telling you about his concern in this matter?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I ask you to turn to your second binder, I am sorry to ask you to juggle, and to turn to tab 50, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Rule 65 ter 1D663. It has an ERN 1D00-5898, and there is no Macedonian translation.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, which tab?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will go through this. It is it again, you will agree, an investigator's note it is dated the 7th of Match of 2002. The time is 1.00, and the purpose of the meeting is to introduce and discuss the draft copy of the operational order for the exhumation project at Ljuboten. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can turn to the last page, can you confirm that this note was prepared by you?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the list of persons present during that meeting, you have, again, Mr. Dragoljub Cakic, the deputy public prosecutor of Skopje II regional court; a person called Jani Nica, who is a judge at the primary court in Skopje II; Mr. Dragan Nikolovski, the investigative judge of primary court Skopje II; Mr. Szydlik, your colleague, who was an operations officer of the ICTY field office; yourself; and Ms. Brajovic, your interpreter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, as can be seen from both the title of this document and the first paragraph of the document, the purpose of the meeting was to discuss a draft plan for the exhumation which you and your colleague, Mr. Eamon Smith, had prepared for the Ljuboten exhumation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention to the second paragraph in that document, it says this: "The investigative judge," which would be Mr. Nikolovski, "spoke of the potential security concerns that he and his colleagues had over the exhumation project. He reinforced that all were willing to undertake the responsibility. However, he wished to stress that fears he referred to related to the security of all those -- all of those present during the on-site operation." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And does that accord with your memory of what Judge Nikolovski said at the time?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also correct that during this meeting, and during other meetings, you indicated that the issues of security and the security concern of the participants would be raised with international organisations, in particular NATO and the OSCE? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct that these concerns, the security concerns which were mentioned to you both in November of 2001 and March of 2002, still existed at the time in Macedonia in September of 2002, when the Prosecution applied to have the case referred to its jurisdiction? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is difficult for me to answer because I finished my responsibilities on site, if I might say, in May -- April/May of 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In that case, I will inflict additional juggling on you, Mr. Tucker, and if I can ask to you back to the first of your binder and to turn to tab 26, please. This is, again, Rule 65 ter 1D638.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is, again, the transcript of the deferral hearing in this and other cases. And with the registry's assistance, I would like to see page 17 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So tab 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I could ask to you go to page 17 of the -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will draw your attention to line 8 of page 17. Those are the comments of Mr. Dzikov who represented the Macedonian authorities during that hearing. And on the 25th of September of 2002, Mr. Dzikov said this: "Still, there is we well-founded fear that the security situation in the Republic of Macedonia and the unstable peace that was established after last year's armed clash caused by the terrorist criminal gangs that are still operating in the Republic of Macedonia could be disrupted if these cases would be tried by the Macedonian courts." Would you agree that the concerns expressed to you earlier were, again, reiterated in this particular instances by Mr. Dzikov and, in particular, as regard the cases in question?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I ask to you go to tab 24 of this binder, this is Exhibit P391. And I will direct yourself to, again, annex H. This would be N00-9883-38 [sic]. N000-9883-38. Mr. Tucker, this is, again, a letter which we have briefly seen earlier. And I won't go through the entirety of this document at this stage, but simply ask you to turn to the last page of that document, where the signature of Mr. Dzikov appears.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that page 59, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be N000-9883-41, on the top right-hand corner of the document.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if can I draw your attention to the third paragraph on that page, this is what Mr. Dzikov wrote to Madam Del Ponte: "The security situation in Republic of Macedonia, even after 26 September 2002, is still endangered by constant attacks of persons that use violence for political goals. There are still murders of civil persons and members of the security forces, kidnapping of civil persons, violent acts from the Albanian terrorist gangs which call themselves "Army of Republic," "Ilirida" [phoen], and ANA, Albanian Liberation Army, and terrorist gangs from the protectorate Kosovo, FRY, which illegally legal enter the Republic of Macedonia and are a permanent threat and real danger for the security, and, at the same time, these are serious invitations of international humanitarian law." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then Mr. Dzikov goes on to say: "Because of this critical condition of the state, the postponing of the prosecution and the hesitancy of the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY and the ICTY, which lead to expansion of terrorism and serious violations of international humanitarian, and in order to reconcile the legal views regarding the exercise of primacy, I consider that there is a need of an urgent joint working meeting with you and the president of the ICTY, Judge Claude Jorda." Mr. Tucker, were you aware of the fact that Mr. Dzikov had complained about the hesitance of your office in relation to these matters?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware that Mr. Dzikov was not the only representative of the Macedonian authorities that had complained about the hesitancy of your office, but that Professor Duma, the head of the Forensic Institute, had made such a complaint? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I was not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I ask you to turn to your second binder, Mr. Tucker, and to look at tab 60. It is Exhibit P2898. It is a Prosecution exhibit. If you can look at the first page, Mr. Tucker, at first, this is a document that comes from the university, the Medical Faculty of the University, and more specifically the Forensic and Criminology Institute. It is dated the 22nd of May 2003, and it is sent to Mr. Nikolovski, Dragan. And if you look at the second page of that document, you will see it is signed by Mr. Duma, Professor Duma. I will just read to you the last paragraph of that document. It says this: "Besides this situation, professional staff of the Forensic Institute recommend that further delay of the commencement of the activities of the ICTY in analysing the concrete even might have negative repercussions over the Macedonian state, and, therefore, it was decided to provide the requested documentation to the authorised court, in hope that the authorised institutions and bodies of the state will provide conditions for further work and existence of the institute in all its segments." Were you aware of that document, or in any case, of the matter raised by Mr. Duma about delays in the commencement of ICTY activities?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of neither the document or the comment, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, also for the record and concerning the issue of security in Macedonia during the relevant period, I will draw Your Honour's attention to paragraph 18, 1-8, of the Trial Chamber's decision on deferral, which is at tab 37 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, can you confirm that another matter which was raised by the Macedonian authorities during your meetings, quite frequently in relation to the investigation, was the problems which they encountered because of the lack of cooperation of the ethnic Albanian community, or at least part of that community. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall, in particular, or perhaps I will ask you about the particular incident. Do you recall that these particular concerns were raised, in particular, in relation to the Neprosteno and Ljuboten investigations?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd ask you to go back to your first binder, Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could bring up Rule 65 ter 1D613. That's the document under tab 31 of your binder. I'm sorry. This has been MFI'd as 1D197.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is, again, Mr. Tucker, the same investigator's notes that we have seen on a number of occasion before, but I would like you to turn to the second page of that document and to the fourth paragraph on that page. Those are comments attributed to Mr. Cakic, the public prosecutor, and he said this: "They have not been able to visit the scene of the killings, to conduct an on-site investigation or visit the site of the graves of the victims. No interviews had been conducted with the relatives of the victims or any other investigation with other potential witnesses. (Security concerns)." Do you recall that Mr. Cakic explained to you that they had been unable to interview relatives because of the security concerns.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Tucker, that the Macedonian police had, in fact, attempted unsuccessfully to obtain information from villagers as to the identity of the deceased?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was aware that the investigative judges had tried, and I assume that would have been with the support of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that the villagers refused to provide that assistance to the police?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My knowledge was refusal to give the information to the investigative judges, which may or may not be the same things.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will simply indicate for the record or draw attention of the Chamber to Exhibit P104 and Exhibit 1D190, on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, in the course of those meetings, do you remember a particular occasion where the state prosecutor, Mr. Dzikov, had underlined, once again, the unwillingness of the Albanians to provide them with information pertaining to these particular investigations, Neprosteno and Ljuboten? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to go backward in your binder to tab 29, this is Rule 65 ter 1D612. It is MFI'd as 1D196. This is one of your investigator's notes. It records a meeting of the 27 of November of 2001 with Mr. Dzikov and one of his assistants. I would like to draw your attention, more specifically, to the next page -- well, sorry, Mr. Tucker. Perhaps, we'll go first on the first page simply to record the fact this fact: "The public prosecutor," that's the first paragraph, "welcomed the representative of the ICTY. He stated that he was surprised to hear that the Prosecutor had only opened investigation into two cases, Neprosteno and Ljuboten." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if you look at the second paragraph: "He stressed the view of the Prosecutor," and that's Mr. Milner speaking. "He stressed the view of the Prosecutor that Macedonia was a sovereign state and had the responsibility and compatibility to investigate crimes of this nature. He stated that it was not within the mandate of the Tribunal to interfere with that judicial process." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then in the next sentence, you record an agreement between the parties present that: "It was agreed that it would not be beneficial to rush any of the investigations." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can now turn to the second page, please, Mr. Tucker, I'd like to draw your attention to the second paragraph on that document, which started with the word, the "PP." That would be the public prosecutor. Mr. Dzikov said this: "The public prosecutor stated that whatever the outcome of the investigations, the Macedonian authorities are placed -- pleased with the involvement of the ICTY as an independent investigative body. There followed some debate concerning, A, the build up of the tension in the area of the exhumation, arrest of any suspects, the kidnapping of civilians, and the murder of three police officers; and, B, the problems of obtaining details of crimes from Albania witnesses." Do you remember Mr. Dzikov telling you this?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall also that Mr. Dzikov indicated to you that that one particular problem in investigating that sort of case involving Albanian witnesses was the brutal ways or manners of the NLA. Do you recall him tell you that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look at the paragraph in this same document which starts with the word "PP" and "DM." "So public prosecutor and Dennis Milner discussed the operational difficulties in obtaining the cooperation of Macedonian Albanian population, NLA tactics of amongst other fear and extortion." Do you recall that discussion between Mr. Dzikov and Mr. Milner?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree, I hope, that the NLA, in fact, did not hesitate to use violent means to prevent investigations. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly do, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the reference to the three policemen earlier in the documents that had been killed, you would agree that those three policemen were three policemen sent to Neprosteno to protect the exhumation site, is that correct, and they were killed by the NLA?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. The incident occurred the day before the first date of the exhumation at Neprosteno.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you also aware of the fact that on at least one occasion the NLA threatened to blow up courtrooms in Skopje? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And they made that threat in relation to the persons that had been arrested during the Ljuboten incident; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you also recall a particular meeting with Prosecutor Cakic where he highlighted the difficulties to obtain information and cooperation from the Albanian community? And what I'm more interested in: Can you recall that the Prosecution, Cakic, underlined the importance of the involvement of the OTP to assist with obtaining that information?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir. I think it is fair to say that in relation to both the exhumations of the feeling of the Macedonian authorities of the importance of the -- the attendance of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask, perhaps, to look at another one of your investigator's note, Mr. Tucker. This is under tab 34 of your binder. This is it Rule 65 ter 1D615. Mr. Tucker, as you can see, this is another one -- or I'll ask you to confirm, this si another one of the investigator's notes prepared by you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is about a meeting arranged by Mr. Szydlik for the visit of Mr. Milner, and the meeting took place on the 29th of November 2001 in the office of the deputy primary public prosecutor in Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to turn to the next page, to the fourth paragraph, in particular, of that document, which started with the words: "Mr. Sokic," which is, in fact, Mr. Cakic. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says: "Mr. Cakic then spoke at length about the closeness of the Albanian community and the difficulties experienced in obtaining information from one Albanian about another. However, it was his belief, and that of his colleagues, that the community would speak to representatives of the ICTY because of a trust that Macedonians have generally in the work of the Tribunal. He also reaffirmed the willingness and wish of himself and his colleagues to carry out the responsible of their office. "He stated that the investigative judge had already accepted the facts relating to five victims, and he believed that the investigative judge had already been in contact with Professor Duma at the Forensic Institute." Mr. Tucker, does that, again, accord with your memory of this particular meeting or generally with the meeting you had with the authorities?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall another occasion when Prosecutor Cakic explained to you that this lack of cooperation and lack of trust on the part of the -- or at least a part of the Albanian population of Macedonia towards the authorities extended to things such as providing information for post-mortem examinations in the context of criminal proceedings? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to look at tab 50, 5-0, in your second binder, Mr. Tucker, this would be Rule 65 ter 1D663. This is a meeting -- or the record of a meeting which we have already seen, Mr. Tucker. It is dated the 7th of March 2002 in the Prosecution public office, and, again, present are Mr. Cakic, Jani Nica, Nikolovski, Szydlik, yourself, and your translator, Ms. Brajovic. And I would like you to turn to the second page, please, and to the second paragraph in particular, where Mr. Dragoljub Cakic is recorded as saying the following: "Dragoljub Cakic raised the point that even during peacetime the Albanian community never consented to post-mortem examination of the dead, including instances of homicide. He queried the consent provided by the relatives of the deceased for such an operation to proceed now." Do you recall Mr. Cakic raising this question with you?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go to the next paragraph, we'll see you gave an answer to Mr. Cakic at the time. It says: "Howard Tucker stated that, to his knowledge, these issues had been approached with the relatives from an early stage. He said that family had agreed to the procedure, as long as the ICTY closely monitored all stages of the investigation." Is that in fact what you answered Mr. Cakic at that time?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can go further down in that document in the passage that starts: "Because of the unique aspects." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will trade for the transcript. It says: "Because of the unique aspect of this case, and as a result of several meetings with the ICTY and the office of the public prosecutor of Macedonia, the above-named court official are aware that such information should be forthcoming as a result of the current initiative; that is, the forthcoming ICTY meeting with the relatives of the families. The court has appointed the above-named individuals to supervise the investigation; however, in order for the investigation to proceed in accordance with the law, they urgently require certain information. "The very least that is required at this stage are the names and details of the deceased, where they died, and the dates of death, if possible. Once that is completed, the relevant official can request the services of the Forensic Institute and the department -- once that is completed, the relevant official can request the services of the Forensic Institute and the Department of Criminal Technology. In reality, they are already informed of this, but they require the other details in order to complete the official 'route.'" Can you recall that exchange during the meeting, Mr. Tucker?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that because of the inability of the Macedonian authorities to obtain that information directly from the families of the victims, Mr. Szydlik, your colleague, in fact, took care of this? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my recollection, yes, he, with the assistance of others.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were aware also that, as we have just read, without this particular information, the procedure in Macedonia could not legally go forward? Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And they also made it clear to you at the time that, once they would obtain that information from you, they would be able and were willing to move forward with the investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, perhaps, I will ask you to look at tab 49 of your binder. This is Rule 65 ter number 1D662. This is another one of investigator's notes, Mr. Tucker. The purpose of this meeting, according to the document, was to appraise the department of the proposed plan from the exhumation of ten individuals from the cemetery in the village of Ljuboten. The meeting took place on 7 March 2002 at 1020, in the Department of Criminal Technology in Skopje, and present were Miroslav Uslinovski, the chief of the Department of Criminal Technology; Simon Dzidrovski head of the identification unit of the Department of Criminal Technology; Ms. Jova Kadrajovic [phoen], translator; and yourself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I could ask you to turn to the fourth page of that document, the last page of the document, to confirm that the note was prepared by you?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do so confirm, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention to the passage which is under the highlighted title, "Concerning obtaining official document such as birth certificate, death certificate, and medical records." There's a statement attributed to yourself which reads as following: "HT," Howard Tucker, "stated that the investigative judge had stated the following: 'If the details of the deceased full names were obtained, including information of the date and place of birth, father's name, if the address of the deceased at the time of death were also included, and whether the deceased was a Macedonian citizen.'" And would appear to reflect or to refer to the previous meeting that we've looked at; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then you say: "Then it would then be possible for the judicial court authorities through official channels to obtain all the relevant documentation in the correct manner, highlighted. Therefore the question of admissibility would not arise." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct, in fact, that you had discussions with the judicial authorities at the time, in particular as relating to concerns that, unless the material was obtaining legal matter, it would not be admissible in court. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that the families of the victims had agreed to the exhumation only under the conditions that you, the Office of the Prosecutor, would be present during the entire exhumation process and would closely monitor each stage of the process of exhumation an autopsy? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to embark on a slightly different topic, and I wonder if that is a proper time. If it is not, I will go on, Your Honour. Your Honour, I will certainly continue until half past.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, is that also correct that during one of the meetings which you had with the competent authorities, in particular with Prosecutor Cakic, that he had asked you to convince the villagers to talk to them? "Them" being the judicial authorities. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that your initial response at that time was that you had preliminary information, which suggested that the villagers would be unwilling to do so? Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir. I think it was also unwilling for them to travel to Skopje to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Could you please turn to tab 50 of the binder please. It is, again, Rule 65 ter 1D663.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to move to page 5 of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is the same -- one of the notes that we have already had a look at, Mr. Tucker. And if can I draw your attention to the section of the document that starts under the title: "Other matters. In this note, you recorded the following: "Dragoljub Cakic stated that ordinarily relatives of the deceased and other witnesses would come before the investigative judge and make a statement about the events under oath. This statement would contain much of the information necessary to speedily advance the investigation. Many of the potential difficulties could be overcome if this procedure could be followed." "Dragoljub Cakic accepted the difficulties involved and the likelihood that the relatives and other witness would refuse to cooperate and probably refuse to come to the court building. He stated that the court could grant an assortment of security guarantees, including closed session hearings with full protective measures. He followed this by saying that the only person present would be the investigative judge and a court clerk." And then you're responded in the following terms: "Howard Tucker replied by saying that he had not spoken to the witnesses of family members, but the investigator stated that he had information that suggested that Dragoljub Cakic was correct in this belief that they, the relatives of the deceased, would not be willing to come to court to swear their statements. "However, Howard Tucker asked if it were possible for investigative judge and court official to travel to another location and to receive/accept the statements under oath in a non-court building. "Dragoljub Cakic stated that this was possible, though unusual. Special judicial approval would have to be applied for and granted, prior to such an event occurring." Does that accord with your memory of this exchange Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you then, you and your colleague, Mr. Szydlik, met and talked to a number of representatives from the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also correct that, as had been foreseen by you during the particular meeting we discussed, the family of the victims refused to go to the court in Skopje to give a statement to the Macedonian authorities?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the families of the victims requested that or agreed that any such meeting will have to take place in a different location; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And they agreed to be interviewed by the investigative judge at the field office -- or I'm sorry, the headquarters of the OSCE in Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. On a time-line, sir, I had already approached this subject with Susan Ringgaard in relation to the possibilities of using the OSCE premises to obtain her agreement in principle to that being able to take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I am grateful for this, Mr. Tucker. Is that correct also that one of the conditions that were set by the villagers, to agree to talk to the investigative judge, was that a representative of your offers, the Office of the Prosecutor, should be present during those interviews? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, Mr. Szydlik your colleague, the operation officer, accompanied the villagers to all of the interviews and was present during the meetings with the investigative judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, rather than going through each and every one of those documents, I will simply record the relevant court records. This is under tab 52, following of Your Honours's binder, and it has the following numbers: ET-N002-1210 -- they all part of P55. It is ET-N002-1210; ET-N002-1212; ET-N002-1214; ET-N002-1216; ET N002-1208; ET N002-1220; ET-N002-1222.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also, Mr. Tucker, that this meeting of, I believe, 8th of March 2002 was the first such meeting which you had with the villagers of Ljuboten? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the purpose of this meeting was to discuss, once again, the operational plan for the exhumation at the cemetery in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if that can be of assistance to you, Mr,. Tucker I will draw your attention to tab 51 of your binder, which is already an exhibit as 1D9.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Tucker, that it took quite a bit of convincing on your part and the promise that the OTP would be involved in all stages of the process and that there would be no police present in the village for the representatives to agree to the exhumation operation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your note, I believe, you indicated that at the time there was, what you term, I believe, "a huge mistrust of anything Macedonian on the part of the Ljuboten villagers." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps, rather than paraphrasing you, I will ask to you look at the third page of this documentary.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask you, again, to confirm this is note prepared by yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the meetings with the representatives of the village took place on the 8th of March 2002; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it took place in the school in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you could you turn to the third page after that document, the last page, you discuss, in this note, various matters pertaining to the exhumation and autopsy, and if I can draw your attention starting with the words, "Anyway." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall that one of the issues that raised difficulties with the families was the suggestion, or the possibility in any case, that the bodies that were to be exhumed in Ljuboten might have to spend some time in the Forensic Institute for storage purposes. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that the family refused that the bodies be stored at the Forensic Institute, that they opposed that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially, they did, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then, at the time that you made the note, as followed, you said: "They still carry a huge mistrust of anything Macedonian." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that accords with your memory of this particular meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct or is it within your knowledge that none of the villagers brought criminal charges against any, anyone for that matter, any member of any ministry or any person that might have been involved in the operation? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that your colleague, Mr. Szydlik, had suggested to the villagers that they should bring criminal charges?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is another matter which I would like to ask, which is related, again, to the issue of security in Macedonia at the time, and in particular in relation to the Ljuboten investigation and Neprosteno investigation. Are you aware of the fact that one of the particular difficulties involved in the investigative process in Macedonia, in relation to these cases, was the absence of a system of witness protection in the country at the time? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware also that the Chief Prosecutor Madam Del Ponte raised this particular issue as one of the reasons justifying the deferral of the cases, including Ljuboten, to the jurisdiction of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps, I can assist, if you are good enough to go back to your first binder, Mr. Tucker. And I will ask to you go to tab 26 of this binder. This is Rule 65 ter 1D638, and this is, again, the transcript of the deferral hearing of 25th September 2001.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can turn to page 6 of this transcript, Madam Del Ponte was asked to explain the reasons or the basis for her application to have these five cases including Ljuboten referred to the jurisdiction of the Tribunal. I will come back on some other aspects of her submissions; but, at this stage, I will draw your attention to the first line of page six. It say this, and those are submissions made by Madam Del Ponte during the hearing: "In Macedonian law, the protection of witnesses is not provided for. It is not provided for in Macedonian law, but that's absolutely vital, essential, for these investigations to be successful." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I can, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were you aware of those particular statements made by Madam Del Ponte?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to turn to page 34 of that same document, please.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: At this time, Mr. Tucker, if you look at the previous page those submissions are the submissions of Mr. Dzikov during the same hearing?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Mr. Dzikov said the following, it starts at the top of page 34. He said: "I would like to inform you on something else regarding the other two cases, that there were mass graves in the village of Neprosteno and the village of Ljuboten. It is the unknown perpetrators, unidentified perpetrators. We have not identified the perpetrators. I would like to ask you that these two cases are investigated by the prosecution before the competent court, the Tetovo court related to the Neprosteno case, where there is a mass grave, and it is a case against an unidentified perpetrator. "The second case that my esteemed Prosecutor colleague discussed," if can you turn to the next page "the case of the Ljuboten victim, the second mass graves where also an exhumation has been performed. I inform you, respecting both Article 18 from the Statute and Article 8 from the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, are fully and simultaneously, together with us, we have conducted investigations related to the exhumations, so that we, as authorities, the judicial authorities, made no obstacle to the performance of the investigations by the colleague, Prosecutor." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then Mr. Dzikov goes on to say: "Furthermore, as you have heard in my proposal, we are at the disposal to cooperate before -- because it is severe crimes in violations of international humanitarian law. That is all about. I would, once again, like to stress, regarding the victims and the witnesses, as I mentioned, we have no temporary legal protection and, therefore, it could happen that the witnesses and victims as well could be blackmailed or forced, induced not to appear before the Macedonian courts. And for these reasons, in my proposal, I explained what could happen in the future, what could be the fate of the victims and the witnesses and also the cause of the court procedures." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were you aware that Mr. Dzikov had taken a position similar to that of Madam Del Ponte, to the effect that such cases, if tried and prosecuted in Macedonia, could carry serious risks for the victims and witnesses?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, I will also draw Your Honour's attention to the decision on the Trial Chamber, to the decision on deferral of 4 October 2002, in particular to paragraph 13 where those submissions have recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And is that now a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will then adjourn now, to resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, you will recall that, yesterday, I showed you a number of documents and information that established that the Chief Prosecutor, Madam Del Ponte, had announced that she had opened a formal investigation into the events of Ljuboten on the 9th of November, 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you had indicated, I believe, at the time you were not aware the exact date when that was done; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you were aware, Mr. Tucker, I believe, of the fact that back in November 2001, a team of the Office of the Prosecutors had been set up to look into these two cases. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that particular time, there actually wasn't any team set up as such. It was the investigative team leader, Mr. Matti Raatikainen, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I ask to you look, perhaps, at your first binder, please, Mr. Tucker, under tab 27. That would be Exhibit 1D35.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which tab, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: 27, please.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this is -- again, we've seen it already, Mr. Tucker. I don't want to go through the complete text again. This is a record of a meeting with representatives of the OSCE. Do you recall that document?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can to you look at the last page of that document and you recall this meeting related to Neprosteno and Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I ask you to look at the second paragraph on the last page of that document, there's a statement attributed to your colleague, Dennis Milner, and I will read it tout you. It says this: "Dennis Milner stated that he would recommend a full and open investigation. He stated that one of the investigation teams had already been allocated the responsibility to investigate the issues discussed at this meeting, Team O7, Matti Raatikainen and that senior trial attorney, had been appointed to review the cases under investigation," then a there is a parenthesis saying "AC." Do you agree that the senior trial attorney referred to with an "AC" should be Andrew Cayley?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You could agree that on the basis of what Mr. Milner said at the time, in fact, an investigation team had been allocated the responsibility to investigate issues discussed at the meeting in question?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And the membership was Matti Raatikainen and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Mr. Cayley as the attorney, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I ask you to turn to the next document under tab 28 of your binder, that's MFI'd as 1D195. And this is, again, the record of one of those meeting, this time with the then Macedonian minister of the justice. And I would like to draw your attention to the second paragraph of that first page, where Mr. Milner said the following: "Dennis Milner stated that it was his responsibility to assess the current situation in Macedonia related to the investigations into the Neprosteno and Ljuboten. He explained that the ICTY realised that there were more cases than these; but, in respect of them, a dedicated investigation team had been appointed by the Prosecution ICTY to assess the available evidence." So you will agree, Mr. Tucker, once again, that what Mr. Milner says is that, at that stage, a team of the Office of the Prosecutor had been assigned the responsibility to review the material the in your possession in relation to both Neprosteno and Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. At that time, as I said, it was the team of myself and Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that time would be the 27th of November 2001, when this announcement was made in any case?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you will agree that, although the official announcement of the opening of a formal investigation was made by Madam Del Ponte on the 20th or 21st of November of 2001, in fact, the investigation of the Prosecution and the collection of information by the Office of the Prosecutor had started much earlier than that? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think on the basis of the documents that you showed my through the course of my examination, that would be true, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can recall, you will agree that at least one of those documents was dated the 15th of August of 2001, which would be only a day or two after the events; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that your investigation into the events of Ljuboten at the time had involved the taking of, or in any case the interviewing of, potential witnesses? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At what stage, sir? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will specify. Would you agree that as early as the end the month of August 2001, that would be a fortnight after the events, your office had started interviewing potential witness? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe we saw Mr. Raatikainen had interviewed some, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you agree that Mr. Raatikainen, in fact, interviewed two such persons: Mr. Fatmir Etemi, an Albanian member of parliament and Mr. Avdil Aliu, a villager from Ljuboten? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter would kindly like to ask the speakers to make pause between questions an answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, we are not pausing apparently between question and answer, which we can agree to, I believe. Can you agree that the interview which was taken of Mr. Etemi, the member of parliament, was taken by your colleague, Mr. Raatikainen, on the 30th of August of 2001 and 1st of September of 2001?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I have seen the document for that so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps, I can assist you, Mr. Tucker. If you can turn to tab 2 of your binder, number 2, please, it is Rule 65 ter 1D382. And, as you can see, this is a regular or typical OTP witness statement of, in this case, Mr. Fatmir Etemi. And if you can take a look at the date of the interview, you will see it is the 30th of August 2001 and the 1st of September 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look to the next tab, tab number 3, which would be 65 ter 1D607, this is a statement of Mr. Avdil Aliu. The date of the interview taken by Mr. Matti Raatikainen was the 31st of August 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I suppose these two persons were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor based or as a result in part of the information which had within available to you prior to that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would assume that to be the case, but I had no involvement or knowledge of that at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I can assist, Mr. Tucker, in relation to this matter. Would you agree that the belated announcement by the Office of the Prosecutor -- and by "belated," I mean until the end of November 2001. The belated announcement by the Office of the Prosecutor of the commencement of an investigation into the events of Ljuboten was, in part, based on the fact of fear of the reaction that could be triggered in Macedonia after the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement; is that something you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I would be able to comment on the decision of the Prosecutor to open the investigation, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of requests, or in any case indications, being given by certain states to your office to the effect that the announcement of an investigation into the events of Ljuboten should be considered very carefully, in view of the fact of the sensitive political situation in the region at that time? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am, sir. That was raised, if I remember correctly, at some of the meetings that I attended at the end of November 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are aware that, in fact, the matter had been raised earlier on with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps, I can assist. If you could look at tab 43 of your binder, Mr. Tucker, please, that would be in the second binder. This is Rule 65 ter 1D649.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we move into private session. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, I'll go with you through this document briefly. You can see, as I indicated -- have indicated earlier, the origin of this document. Its date is the 24th of August of 2001, a week or so after the events. The subject is ICTY in Macedonia, and the summary is: "Read out on cross Whitehall meeting on role of ICTY in Macedonia way forward with ICTY and Ljuboten incident." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can turn to the next page of that document already, and to point 3 in particular, it reads as follows: "Grateful, therefore, if you would make the point in paragraph 4 below to your ICTY contacts. The Whitehall meeting agreed that an ICTY role in Macedonia could be a deterrent. It would be useful if we and others let it be known that ICTY were watching the actions of both sides very carefully. ICTY were clearly going to go ahead with information gathering in Macedonia. "The legal threshold for formally opening an ICTY investigation, widespread and systematic crimes against humanity committed as part of an armed convict, would have to be met if ICTY eventually opened an investigation in and put significant resources into Macedonia. The political consequences of announcing publicly an investigation into Ljuboten would have to be considered carefully if it came to that." Can read this?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can down a few paragraphs, there is a paragraph starting with the words "However." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says: "However, the situation in Macedonia is extremely tense, delicate political balance at the moment. ICTY will need to think carefully about the impact of any announcements of an investigation on stability in the region. Timing at the moment - just as NATO go in - could be awkward, linking ICTY to the NATO in the minds of outsiders." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
