utterances.text: And were you aware at the time of representations of this particular government of any other government to your office in line with these comments?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I think it is fair to say to that the level of this particular document, if it was made public to the Tribunal, would have been to the Prosecutor or that level within the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you say the "Prosecutor," that would mean Madam Del Ponte; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply to ask to you look at another paragraph further down in this document: "Given that ICTY's mandate is limited area of sustained armed conflict, have you taken a view on when or whether an armed conflict can be said to have begun in Macedonia." Were you aware of such queries being made by certain government with the office at this time?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is unclear to the Prosecution just what the relevance of these comments by someone in the government of the United Kingdom are to the issues present in case. I am wondering if my colleague could explain that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, perhaps, could the witness be excused, perhaps, for this response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you might waiting just outside the door.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MS. METTRAUX
utterances.text: : Thank you, Your Honour. Well, the relevance of this document, Your Honour, is to establish that, contrary to the original evidence of this witness, he has come around to agreeing that the investigation of the Office of the Prosecutor had, in fact, started much earlier than he believed at first. What the Defence submit is that the investigation of the Prosecution started very earlier on in the procedure, as early as perhaps one or two days after the events. What we will indicate at a later stage is that the Prosecution started collecting material, started taking statements from witnesses, and did not in any way share the fruit of this investigative work at any stage with the Macedonian authority. Another issue of relevance is the time at which the Office of the Prosecutor effectively exercised his or her primacy in this matter. And one issue which will be explored with the witness in question is the issue of primacy and when the Prosecutor, in fact, started to take over this investigation. Mr. Saxon was kind enough to indicate prior to the commencement of this hearing that there will be further material closed to us, this in the course of the afternoon, which go in the same direction and which further relate to that matter. And we have reason to -- to believe, again, and my colleague will correct me if I'm wrong, that the effective seizing of the investigation into Ljuboten by the Office of the Prosecutor may have taken place much earlier than what this witness believed originally and what some of the documents may suggest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, how does this particular document have a relevance sufficient to justify its admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we believe that the relevance of this is twofold. One, on the one hand, it explains the reason why the Prosecution waited another three months, from August to November of 2001, to effectively announce that she had openly started an investigation. The second one, and we will continue to explore this matter through other documents relating to one, concerns the issue of the armed conflict and the question of government in relation to this matter. Furthermore, and before my colleague can start answering, there's also the indication, Your Honour, about the sensitive or fragile security situation in the country, which is highlighted yet again in this document. That may not be the most important part of that document, since it has been highlighted in many other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if there is an issue reflected in this document as to why the Prosecution waited from August to -- from August of 2001 to November of 2001 to announce that it had started an investigation, then I think that question needs to be put to this witness. I don't see the relevance of that question emanating from this document. Regarding the issue of armed conflict, we see a question on the bottom of page two in this document referring to the ICTY's mandate limited to areas of sustained armed conflict, and then a question by the author to the reader about the -- whether there was an armed conflict or not in Macedonia. But that is simply a question made by one party to another party, and the Prosecution does not see how that would advance the issues of this case. Regarding the sensitive security situation in Macedonia at this time, what we see here is really in the middle of page 2 a paragraph saying, suggesting that the ICTY will need to think carefully about the impact of any announcement of an investigation on stability in the region. This seems to be, Your Honour, political speculation about political consequences of decisions that might be made by the ICTY, or not. And, in the Prosecution's view, this does not advance the issues raised in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D204, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could we have the witness back, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, I apologise for the inconvenience. Going back to the problems that you indicated existed in obtaining the cooperation of the Albanian families or some Albanian families to cooperate with the Macedonian authorities, is that correct that you look for alternative ways to obtain information pertaining to the Ljuboten investigation?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And these efforts included efforts to obtain ante-mortem datas about the deceased: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you obtained that information through and with the assistance of the OSCE; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of the other reasons -- you have indicated that one of the reasons for your effort, if I wish to go through the OSCE to obtain such information, was the difficulties for the security forces or the police or other authorities to obtain that sort of the cooperation. Another reason that I put to you is that the security forces at the time were perceived by you - and I mean the Office of the Prosecutor not yourself, Mr. Tucker - but were perceived by your office as having a vested interest, if I wish, in this matter since they had been accused of committing crimes in Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. As an additional element as well which with your permission I will say.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I referred to it earlier, and that was the belief that if the security forces of Macedonia were used to secure the area for the exhumation, then that in itself might have been confrontational and reactivated the armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, you made a record of this in one of your notes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I may ask you to turn to tab 49 of your binder, I would like to show you one of those records. This is the record of a meeting that took place, again, on the 7 March 2002, 1520, Department of Criminal Technology.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. This is Rule 65 ter 1D662, tab 49.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, this is the meeting with Mr. Uslinovski and Mr. Dzidrovski. And if I can ask you to turn to the second page after that document, and ask you to look at the paragraph which started with the word, "HT stated that he told the judiciary." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you recorded yourself as stating the following: "Howard Tucker stated that he told the judiciary that due to the publicity about this incident, the security forces of Macedonia could feel that they are already implicated in potential offences; therefore, they have a vested interest in the investigation as a whole. The security forces involved in the incident at Ljuboten were under the authority of the Ministry of Interior." Can you recall making that record in your notes?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you have just mentioned it. But when contacts became necessary to be made with the villagers, the OSCE was the go-between between yourself and the villagers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply for the record, Your Honour, there are indications of this in tab 32, 33, and 34 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that in the course of meetings, which you had are the judicial authorities, you asked those authorities to keep the results, the findings of the exhumation and autopsy away from the Ministry of Interior. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that was again, Mr. Tucker, I suppose, based on the same concern as was just highlighted in the passage that I read to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you queried the possibility of an order being made by court to that effect, to ensure that the material would not be provided to the Ministry of Interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall, during those meetings which you had with the authorities, your colleague, Mr. Milner, indicated on a number of occasion that his view of the investigation, or his view of the manner in which it should be conducted, should be in effect a cooperation between yourself and the Macedonian judicial authorities?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall also that Mr. Milner, during one of those meetings, indicated or highlighted for the judicial authorities the importance for your office, the Office of the Prosecutor, to start collecting material for its own investigation. Do you remember him saying that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, but I can remember the general -- the general concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if I can ask you to go back to the first binder, please, I'll ask you to turn to tab 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is it Rule 65 ter 1D612. It is it MFI'd as 1D196.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, this is one of your three meetings of the 27th of November 2001. This one is, again, with Mr. Dzikov, and we have seen it already. I will ask to you look at that last paragraph on that first page, where Dennis Milner, deputy chief of investigations of the ICTY, says this: "Dennis Milner said that it was essential for the ICTY to gather and assess the available information and evidence. Investigators for the Tribunal would work collectively with the Macedonian agencies." Do you recall Mr. Milner saying that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask to you look at tab 27 briefly of your binder, this is Exhibit 1D35. Again, Mr. Tucker, this is the record of the meeting with the OSCE, 27 of November, and I'll ask you to turn to the third page and last page of the document. And you will recall earlier on, in the discussion that we've had, I read to you a passage by Mrs. Sandra Mitchell, where she asked you to provide assistance and support to the effort by the Macedonian judicial authorities. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the response of Mr. Milner to that suggestion by Ms. Mitchell of the OSCE was the following: "DM," Dennis Milner, "stated that he preferred to think of an open cooperation between the Macedonian judicial authorities and the ICTY lawyers." Do you recall him saying?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps you recall also that during some of those meetings an agreement was reached between the judicial authorities and, in particular, Mr. Dzikov, the public prosecutor, on the one hand, and your office on the other, to the effect that a joint team should be formed to investigate this incident. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, this team was never set up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge. But, of course, as I mentioned earlier, my -- my responsibility ended in about May of 2002 with Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you recall Mr. Dzikov expressing disappointment and frustration at the failure of your office to respond to that original agreement?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to tab 54 of the second binder. This is Exhibit 1D75.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, you will start being familiar with this letter. This is again a letter of Mr. Dzikov to Madam Del Ponte.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask you to turn to the fourth page of that document.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll ask you to focus on the paragraph which starts with the words: "In the meeting held on 8 May 2002," that is the last-but-one paragraph. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Mr. Dzikov said the following to Madam Del Ponte in this letter: "In the meeting held on 8th May 2002 in Skopje between the Chief Prosecutor of The Hague Tribunal and the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia, it was agreed to form an expert team consisted of six experts who, in the Republic of Macedonia, would contact an adequate team to work in relation to the investigation for which -- investigations for which the Prosecutor of The Hague Tribunal was interested, but for this date we were not informed about forming such a team." Does that accord with your memory, sir?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does. However, I know that a Macedonian team was formed by the Office of the Prosecutor in the early part of 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But a common team with the members of the Macedonian authorities was never merged into that team; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, that's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, Mr. Tucker, that the material which we have seen you had started collecting as early as the 15th of August of 2001 was, in fact, never communicated to the Macedonian authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll ask you more specifically about the two statements that we've seen before, the statement of Mr. Etemi and the statement of Mr. Aliu. Would you agree that these two statements were never provided to the Macedonian authorities. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What is the relevance of these questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think I can answer that in front of the witness this time. The suggestion made by Mr. Tucker on a number of occasion was hat originally the Prosecution was assisting or cooperating with the Macedonian authorities. It is also the Prosecution case that the responsibility within investigating this matter was at least, in part, the responsibility of Mr. Boskoski. The documents in question clearly contain material that would have been relevant to any investigation, regardless of who was responsible to conduct this investigation. What we are highlighting at this moment is the fact that this material was never provided to the competent local authorities, and I make it clear that it is no criticism of Mr. Tucker in any way who had no part in deciding the transmission of this document. The reality is that the Prosecution had access to certain information and material which is, was, and should clearly have been identified as relevant and which was never shared by the Prosecution with the local authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I respond, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Of course you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, to the Prosecution's knowledge, there is no legal issue at stake in this case regarding any obligation of the Office of the Prosecutor to provide information to the authorities of Macedonia, including, for example, the accused Mr. Boskoski while he was minister. The -- what is -- what is at issue in this case is whether Mr. Boskoski, under Article 7(3), fulfilled his duty to investigate and punish perpetrators of alleged crimes, and so I don't see how these questions about what the Office of the Prosecutor did or did not do, in terms of transferring information back and forth, are relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We feel, Mr. Mettraux, having looked at the matter somewhat carefully, that it is not an appropriate line of questioning that is being followed at the present time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will simply indicate, perhaps for Your Honours' assistance, that I was about to embark on a related line of questioning which is to the effect that is specific request was made by the local authorities for the support of the Office of the Prosecutor in the provision of material. I agree with Mr. Saxon that the issue in this case is not one of legal obligation or not by the Office of the Prosecutor, and our intention is not to suggest that the Prosecution had in any way an obligation to provide the local authorities. However, what our submissions will be, and we wish to pursue that line of questioning tomorrow, will be that to the extent that a specific request had been made by the local authorities for support and assistance in the form of the provision of documents by the Office of the Prosecutor, which was not acting upon this, had, in effect, a hindering effect on the investigation that was carried out by the local authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Our reaction is to see that as a materially different matter from what you have been pursuing in the last few moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then I should have started by the other issue, Your Honour, but I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
